case.pattern_description: Coordinated cross-account exploitation by a persistent device (Samsung SM-G935F) operating behind anonymous IP proxies. The device systematically targets multiple unrelated cardholder accounts for single or low-frequency card-not-present purchases while evading standard fraud model detection. This repeated abuse spans dozens of cards across multiple months and matches prior confirmed fraud cases classified as an undocumented typology.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3468314 scored 0.006 on the calibrated fraud model with an estimated historical fraud rate of 0.006, and legacy risk score of 0.01.

Transaction 3468314 was conducted online using device D004630 (Samsung SM-G935F on Chrome 62.0 for Android), which was marked as New for the account and operated behind an anonymous IP proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).
Device D004630 was used on 11 cards within the 30-day window, including 10 cards between November 14 and November 18, 2016, with all 11 showing as New devices operating behind anonymous proxies.

All 4 historical closed cases associated with device D004630 (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035) were confirmed fraud classified as undocumented patterns involving unauthorized online purchases via Samsung SM-G935F behind anonymous proxies.

Flagged transaction 3468314 is the first transaction for holder C02910-K1|126|139, showing no prior baseline or recurring history, and deviates from card C02910-K1's primary usage of in-person purchases of product W (60 of 65 past transactions).
Transaction 3468314 occurred in billing region 126, which matches 63 of the 65 historical transactions on card C02910-K1.
Transaction 3468314 was for $224.80 for product C, whereas recent legitimate card activity consisted of smaller in-person product W purchases ($46.41, $58.94, and $136.00).

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Monitoring flagged transaction 3468314 ($224.80) on card C02910-K1 because it originated from device D004630, which is associated with fraud ring 57672119. Although the transaction scored low on standard models and aligned with the card's typical billing region, graph analysis revealed device D004630 appeared as a new device behind anonymous proxies across 11 cards within 30 days, including 10 in a recent four-day burst. Furthermore, all four prior closed cases associated with this device were confirmed fraud classified under an undocumented multi-card exploitation typology. With fraud probability assessed at 0.301, a case has been created, 10 connected cards are placed under monitoring, and the matter is escalated to an analyst for final determination.
